title: First 5 San Francisco: annual audits as the commission recorded them
question: What did the outside auditors report on First 5 San Francisco each year, and how large was the money held in reserve?
finding: The minutes record 6 annual audits (2015-16 to 2020-21). One had a finding: 2018-19, a compliance finding on commissioners' conflict-of-interest filings, reported resolved the next year. The others report no findings. The fund balance printed in the minutes was $29.7 million in 2015-16 and $32.8 million in 2018-19, 1.26 times that year's expenditures; the minutes report it rising again in 2019-20 and 2020-21.
how: Every minutes file was searched for the staff presentation of an annual audit; the issue date, revenues, expenditures, fund balance (or its change) and findings were read from that passage. Where a year appears in several files (draft and final minutes), the passage with the most figures is used.
limits: These are the commission's minutes summarising the audit, not the audit reports. Reserves are expected for a commission funded by a declining tobacco tax (the minutes note the decline) and held for multi-year grants; a large balance is not waste on its own. Blank cells: the minutes did not state the figure.

rows.findings: one compliance finding (conflict of interest filings)

sources.t: First 5 San Francisco (Children and Families Commission): commission and committee agendas and minutes, 2016 to 2022
